title: test_rand_core.rs: RNG via rand_core::TryCryptoRng
description:
Write tests/test_rand_core.rs: test rand_core::TryCryptoRng impl for wolfCrypt RNG.

## What
Verify the RNG trait impl compiles, fills buffers successfully, and produces non-trivially-constant output.

## Algorithm
1. Trait bound proof at compile time:
   fn _assert_try_crypto_rng<R: rand_core::TryCryptoRng>() {}
   fn _check() { _assert_try_crypto_rng::<wolfssl_wolfcrypt::random::Rng>(); }
2. try_fill_bytes basic test:
   let mut rng = Rng::new().expect('RNG init failed');
   let mut buf = [0u8; 32];
   rng.try_fill_bytes(&mut buf).expect('fill failed');
   assert_ne!(buf, [0u8; 32], 'RNG returned all zeros');
3. Successive calls diverge (probabilistic):
   let mut buf1 = [0u8; 32]; let mut buf2 = [0u8; 32];
   rng.try_fill_bytes(&mut buf1).unwrap(); rng.try_fill_bytes(&mut buf2).unwrap();
   assert_ne!(buf1, buf2, 'RNG produced identical successive outputs');
4. PrimInt / generate_block (if exposed by PR #10305):
   Call generate_block::<u8>(), generate_block::<u16>(), generate_block::<u32>(), generate_block::<u64>() and assert Ok.
5. Zero-length fill: rng.try_fill_bytes(&mut []) should return Ok (no crash).

## Defensive rules
- Do not assert any specific byte values from the RNG (DRBG output is not deterministic)
- Probabilistic assertions (buf1 != buf2) have a negligible false-failure rate at 32 bytes; this is acceptable
- Call wolfcrypt_init() before creating any Rng instance
- RNG must be properly cleaned up (Rng type must implement Drop wrapping wc_FreeRng)

## Agent team
- Agent R: read random.rs to confirm exact struct name (Rng? WolfRng?) and which methods are implemented; check if generate_block is added by PR #10305
- Agent I: write test_rand_core.rs per algorithm above
- Agent T: independently verify that rand_core::TryCryptoRng is the current trait name (not RngCore) by checking the rand_core 0.10 changelog

## Tests (oracles)
- No external vector oracle appropriate for DRBG output; tests verify: trait implementation, non-zero output, successive-call divergence, edge cases
- rand_core 0.10 trait hierarchy confirmed from crate documentation (TryCryptoRng = infallible try-fill)
